title: Charred Pepper and Tomato Shakshuka
changes_from_base: Onion, red pepper and fresh chilli are left undisturbed over high heat until they char in spots before the garlic, paprika, cumin and hand-crushed tinned tomatoes go in; six eggs are set into wells around the pan.
summary: Eggs nestled in a deeply charred and tender sauce of peppers, onions and tomatoes, fragrant with cumin and paprika.
equipment: large deep frying pan or sauté pan with a lid

ingredients.item: large red pepper, seeded and thinly sliced
small fresh hot chilli (jalapeño or Fresno), seeded and thinly sliced
tinned whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
fine sea salt or table salt
fresh coriander or parsley (or a mix), chopped

steps.title: Heat Oil
steps.text: Heat 45 ml extra-virgin olive oil in a large deep frying pan or sauté pan over high heat until shimmering.

steps.title: Char Vegetables
steps.text: Add 1 thinly sliced medium onion, 1 large red pepper (thinly sliced) and 1 small fresh hot chilli (thinly sliced) in an even layer and leave untouched about 6 minutes until deeply browned and charred in spots; stir and repeat until soft and charred all over, about 4 minutes more.

steps.title: Spices
steps.text: Add 3 thinly sliced garlic cloves and cook 30 seconds, then add 15 g paprika and 2 tsp cumin seeds (or ground cumin) and stir for 30 seconds, followed immediately by 800 g hand-crushed tinned whole peeled tomatoes.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Simmer very gently for 10 minutes; season with ½ tsp fine salt and ¼ tsp ground black pepper, then stir in half of 15 g fresh coriander or parsley.

steps.title: Eggs
steps.text: Using a large spoon, make 6 wells near the edge, crack 6 large eggs into them and spoon a little sauce over the egg whites, leaving yolks exposed; salt the eggs lightly, cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook 5-8 minutes until the whites are just set and yolks remain runny.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter the remaining herbs over the top and serve straight away with 150 g crusty bread for scooping.

tips: Char the vegetables well before adding the tomatoes for a deeper, smokier flavour base
Make the wells for the eggs just before cracking them in so the sauce stays hot
Runny yolks are not advised for pregnant, very young, elderly or immunocompromised eaters; for them, cover and cook 2-3 minutes longer until the yolks are firm (71 °C)
storage: Serve straight away. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
